chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Said from Ibn Abi Umayr from Hammad from Al-Halabi from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said:

"Any man who has sexual intercourse with a slave woman of a people unlawfully, then buys her and claims her child, then he inherits nothing from her. For the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'The child belongs to the bed (of the father), and for the fornicator is the stone.' And the child of fornication is not inherited except by a man who claims the son of his slave woman.

And any man who acknowledges his child then denies him, it is not for him to do so, and there is no grace/merit by which his child is attached to him if the child is from his wife or his slave woman.'

key_terms.اَلْحَجَرُ: The stone (metaphor for the fornicator having no claim/inheritance)
key_terms.اَلْوَلَدُ لِلْفِرَاشِ: The child belongs to the bed (principle of paternity)

ai.seo_question: What is the inheritance ruling for a master who claims the child of his slave woman after unlawful intercourse?
ai.summary: In the context of *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, this hadith clarifies the inheritance rights of a *walidat*’s child when her master claims paternity after unlawful intercourse (*haram*), emphasizing that mere possession does not confer inheritance without formal acknowledgment (*iqrar*). It reinforces the prophetic maxim 'the child belongs to the bed' (*al-waladu lil-firash*) while noting that a man cannot disown a child he has acknowledged, ensuring lineage stability in Shia jurisprudence.
